headline: Fire department presented a plan to replace police and fire portable radios for a $5,710,975 purchase.
summary: The radios were made in 2015, and the fire department said 7.5% of police radios and 10.6% of fire radios are out of service. After about $335,000 in Fire Department impact fees, the bond would be $5,375,165, paid over FY28 and FY29. The contract goes to committee on December 1st and to the full board on December 15th. The board also voted 7-6 against suspending the rules to pass the kratom ordinance, then voted 13-1 to send it to Bills on Second Reading.
decisions: Failed 7-6: suspending the rules to pass the synthetic kratom ordinance that evening.
Referred the synthetic kratom ordinance to Bills on Second Reading, 13-1.
Confirmed Shirley Tomlinson to the vacant Ward 6 school committee seat, term to expire January 2028.
Approved a review of the Housing Commission's charge after a commission member resigned.
Approved the ordinance amendment on agenda item 24 to pass and be enrolled.
discussion: Radio warranty and parts: Members asked about the three-year warranty on the new radios and whether parts would be available, and the fire department said it expects the radios to last about 10 years.

Synthetic kratom ordinance: Speakers said the product is dangerous and marketed to children, and urged quick action. Members raised questions about the language and debated whether to pass it that night or send it to committee.

Hartnett lot development: Speakers asked how the city would replace about 203 ground-level parking spaces and asked the planning board to require documented answers on safety, access, and snow removal.
Housing Commission complaints: The commission chair said residents have repeatedly complained about conditions and responses at MHRA properties and asked the board to review the complaint process.
2026 tax rate: The assessor said the rate is 14.36, the lowest since records began in 1910, and tax bills go out November 18 and are due December 31.
